correctness.rationale: On f(x)=c||x||²/2, the short BB quotient is exactly 1/c on every nonterminal step. Each of the three AdaBB branches therefore reduces to a dimension-free explicit scalar update. The post-overshoot reset lemma rigorously puts the first later step strictly in (1,2), and subsequent Case II sets normalized step to one. The special initialization yields a_1=1/sqrt2 and a_2²=(1+1/(sqrt2 a_0))/2, proving the exact sharp switch at 1/(7sqrt2) and all seven disjoint startup cases. The uninformed radical factors converge geometrically to phi and have a convergent positive normalized product, proving the exact hitting-count formula and the sharp logarithmic coefficient. Independent high-precision finite simulations support but do not establish continuum claims.

value.rationale: AdaBB explicitly emphasizes lower stepsize bounds and initialization, so the number of updates lost to a tiny initial step is a natural, consequential algorithmic invariant. The complete sharp classification quantifies both an unbounded logarithmic cold-start penalty with universal golden-ratio constant and an initialization-dependent uniform seven-update budget, including a discontinuous exact phase boundary. It distinguishes finite termination from the more routine mere convergence and provides a reproducible baseline on which general conditioning effects can be separated. Narrow scope and comparison to simpler direct BB are explicitly acknowledged.
